A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PowerFlow work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning and creative-writing evaluations, including Table 1, Figures 3–8, and the task-level results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds component ablations, an empirical ranking-inversion measurement, and initialization and compute-cost findings.

M1.justification: The alpha-power target, length-aware Trajectory-Balance loss, format penalty, clipped importance weights, and partition-estimator architecture remain unchanged. v1's final objective, Eq. (9), becomes Eq. (10). Asymmetric clipping and the specialized initialization were already documented in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions retain NuminaMath-CoT training, the same six reasoning benchmarks, and poem continuation, story generation, and joke writing from the same sources. The added diagnostics establish no new dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix D.3 adds the Format-only comparator to the Qwen2.5-Math-7B comparison; v1 evaluated it only for Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B. The comparator memberships in the main reasoning and creative-writing tables otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces component-controlled evaluations, a candidate-pair ranking-inversion metric, and convergence comparisons involving equal versus tripled learning rates. Existing benchmark splits, sampling counts, metrics, and default hyperparameters remain unchanged. The expanded GRPO recipe is additional documentation rather than evidence of a revised main experiment.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanism validation: Appendix D.3 separates length correction from format penalties and tests Format-only at 7B; Appendix E measures ranking inversions; Appendix B reports initialization removal and learning-rate/convergence effects. These address questions beyond the retained objective-comparison curves, alpha sensitivity, solution diversity, and pass@n analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports sampling counts without uncertainty estimates. v2 adds bootstrap SEMs over the 16 samples per problem for PowerFlow–GRPO reasoning averages and component ablations, alongside comparisons against a one-sigma threshold. This introduces uncertainty reporting without establishing additional training runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the creative-writing table, renumbered from Table 2 to Table 3, retain their numerical results. Added findings include 1.5B ablation averages of 14.30 with format correction alone and 33.48 with length correction alone, the 7B Format-only average of 36.22 versus PowerFlow's retained 42.17, and an inversion rate near 0.09. Timing and convergence findings are also newly reported.

T1.justification: v2 adds Propositions 3.2–3.3 and Appendix E: an I-projection characterization, KL-distortion expansion, within-length ranking preservation, pairwise distortion formulas, top-K conditions, and proofs. The retained majority-voting theorem moves from Appendix D to F and gains a full-support assumption, explicit tie-weight accounting, and a compactness argument establishing divergence rather than inferring it merely from positive increments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: unsupervised distribution matching, stable length-aware optimization, reasoning improvements competitive with supervised GRPO, and simultaneous creative quality/diversity gains. The new analyses support these claims without redefining their headline scope.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the largely qualitative defense of length correction with a structured distortion interpretation and qualifies exact semantic recovery as an idealized case requiring the learned multiplier to match the structural bias. It also attributes most ablation gains to length correction, a smaller residual to formatting, and initialization benefits mainly to early optimization.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code/model availability; v2 supplies a code repository link. v2 also documents the DAPO/verl GRPO recipe, answer-verification reward, and compute measurements, including 109.7 versus 100.1 seconds per step on eight H100 GPUs. These disclosures supplement the retained architecture and hyperparameters.

R1.justification: v2 adds DAPO and HybridFlow references supporting its training description and points the Paech citation directly to Creative Writing Benchmark v3. The broader positioning against RLIF, inference-time power sampling, and FlowRL is retained. The extended related-work discussion is relocated, not newly introduced.

P1.justification: The main related-work section is condensed, with its fuller discussion retained in new Appendix A. v2 adds explanatory passages, reorganizes appendix labels, removes the appendix contents page, and adds acknowledgements. Most introductory, experimental, and concluding prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the single-column report layout with a two-column conference layout for the main text and references, substantially reflowing equations, captions, and figures. It adds the component-ablation table and places the retained creative-writing table beneath Figure 8. Existing plots are largely resized or relocated rather than replaced with new results.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports the existing mechanism through component controls and repairs the majority-voting proof's unsupported inference from positive drift to divergence. SEMs and code/compute disclosures improve transparency. The gain is limited by the underspecified ranking-inversion audit and Appendix E's ambiguity between normalized expectations and unnormalized target weights. The principal benchmark findings remain unchanged.
